questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was interested in taking communication classes. Therefore i chose Erasmus University Rotterdam. I also chose the Netherlands because i thought it would be interesting living there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The people working for the exchange office did an introduction meeting and were available to answer any question via email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I didn't have any problems, but the attendance demands for passiing the classes where really strict and some of my friends got into some problems because of that. I felt bad for them because the demands on EUR are so much stricter than at many other universities in the world. There could be better support in relation to having to adapt to another system than what you are used to.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was hard. I ended up finding really good accomodation, but i was more lucky than most. I recommend using Facebook - thats where i found my accomodation. Be aware that there are a lot of scammers, so do not pay anything before having a videocall with the landlord.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That living off campus was in my perspective better than living on campus. It is a good way to get to see other areas of the city and you'll probably live in a more cozy apartment than if you live on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was hard getting accomodation through the university because there just wasn't a lot of student housing available.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration proces went smoothly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could get help from the people in charge of exchange in our faculty.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got some classes i wanted and some i didn't want. I ended up caring way less about the classes than i thought i would both because the way of learning on EUR is way different than in the Danmark(it is more about learning fact than applying what you learn and you have way less academic freedom) and because the subjects just weren't that interesting to me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bear in mind that the classes you can choose from can have very different levels and very different workloads. Do also bear in mind that some classes have mandatory attendance and some don't.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The day- to- day activities in the tutorials where often too easy after i got into the habit of speaking english(i mostly took 1st year courses even though i am a 3rd year student at UCPH). I would have liked to have been challanges more.  In relation to essays and exams, i did fine in all of my classes  so i guess that was a good level for me.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was very different. I definetely prefer the teaching style at home but the one at EUR also had its advantages. At EUR you have to live up to very specific demands and a lot of the exams a focused on you learning things by heart. That was uninspiring to me, while i am used to a lot of academic freedom and the teaching being more focused on applying knowledgde. I did however like the fact that i had a lot of class time compared to at home. It gave me a chance to be social and work on my english. I also liked having smaller assignments than usual, because it makes your life as a student more dynamic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Communication as a Social Force, Communication and Organizations, Consumers Perceptions of Corporate Social Responsibilities, Feeling Orange, Communication Technologies and their Impacts, Intercultural Communication.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: None of the above courses where so interesting to me that i would recommend them to other students.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't encounter any unexpected costs. I did however spend more money than i thought i would.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Being on exchange is generally expensive because you go out a lot and you don't want to miss anything. Expect to spend a lot of money on going out and on travelling. In my opinion these are money well spent.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: ESN offered a lot of activities through which you could meet other exchange - and international students. I was satisfied with the ones i participated in.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Parties, a fitness membership(with access to classes and other sports facilities) and trips to other cities and out of the country.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Participate in as much as possible the first couple of weeks - that's when you meet your friends. Know that a lot of the social activities involves partying, so if you're not a big fan of partying or drinking being on exchange at EUR may not be for you.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend going to France and Belgium because both are so accessible from Rotterdam. Especially Bruges(Belgium) is beautiful. Within the Netherlands i would really recommend going to  Utrecht.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any problems adjusting to dutch culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think that dutch people are a little closed off compared to internationals. I don't think socializing with dutchies where particularly hard but it also wasn't easy.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: See the above answer.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I like the dutch honesty. I lived with two dutch students and i think it made communication easier that they where being frank with me during my time there.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Know that a lot of people you meet are gonna be younger than you. This means that they might be a little less mature but might also be a lot of fun. 2. Don't go for the classes because they are better at UCPH. The culture around education is way more inspiring in Denmark. 3.You will have more class time and less individual work at EUR, which i personally think is preferable for exchange life.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Know that the rules for attendance and assignments are very strict.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The open social environment amongst exchange students. People are very nice and show a lot of interest in you. Meeting people from other countries also opens your mind to other ways of living and to other opportinities than those you normally consider at home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had to get used to having a lot of assignments. In the beginning it was stressful but i got used to it. The overall workload wasn't bigger than what i am used to - just in another form.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
